reviews.reason: This delta delivers the stated capability (order retrieval by returned token, honest not-found/expired-link state, getLastOrder fallback) and the committed-tree browser report confirms it functionally (36/36 PASS, including 'desktop/mobile fresh guest order fetched from Saleor'). However, the clean committed-tree host run still exits 1 ('test-0 exited 1'), and part of that failure is directly attributable to this delta: it adds ORDER_TOKEN_ARG_QUERY ({ order(token: $token) }), a GraphQL document that is permanently invalid against the project's Saleor 3.23 schema and is reported by the host 'storefront GraphQL contract validation' check as 'Unknown argument "token" on field "order" of type "Query"'. It is never reached at runtime (orderByToken succeeds), so it is dead fallback code that only pollutes the contract gate; the sibling invalid lineId selection is pre-existing and not caused by this delta. In addition, the order capability token is now propagated in URL query strings from the payment redirect and account links with no Referrer-Policy configured and no log redaction, exposing a bearer-style credential to browser history and server/proxy access logs, which conflicts with the project's documented 'tokens not written to logs' posture. The core security model is otherwise sound (token-gated access, no order-number enumeration, no auth bypass, anonymous fetch sends no Authorization header, no XSS, currency preserved), but success criterion 4 (committed-tree tests pass) is not met and the new contract violation is a concrete regression introduced here.
blockingRisks: Committed-tree acceptance run is red (test-0 exits 1) and this delta adds a new, always-schema-invalid GraphQL document (order(token:)) flagged by the host 'storefront GraphQL contract validation'; success criterion 4 (committed-tree tests pass) is not satisfied.
Order capability token is placed in URL query strings with no Referrer-Policy or log redaction (medium severity; not the sole blocker).
